sources.title: Sustainable drainage systems
sources.verified_claim: Enfield, as Lead Local Flood Authority and statutory consultee, requires sustainable-drainage strategy information for planning applications and flood-risk assessment where relevant; requirements do not prove drainage capacity at a sample parcel.

sources.title: Havering Infrastructure Planning
sources.verified_claim: Havering's Infrastructure Delivery Plan identifies infrastructure gaps, future needs, indicative costs and funding mechanisms and is described as a live, periodically updated document; plan-level evidence is not parcel utility capacity.

sources.title: Sustainable drainage for major planning applications
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth requires SuDS information for major applications, including layout, runoff calculations, storage, off-site works and maintenance arrangements, and states applications are not valid without required information; validation is not capacity confirmation.

sources.title: Soak up Lambeth SuDS Programme
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth describes a £6 million SuDS programme with Thames Water to reduce flood risk across streets, parks, schools and estates; programme activity is borough resilience context and not evidence that a sample parcel is served by a scheme.

sources.title: What are Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS)?
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth explains SuDS benefits and notes the borough's clay soil limits infiltration and leaves heavy reliance on the combined sewer network; borough geology is not a substitute for site-specific ground and sewer evidence.

sources.title: Chapter 9 Sustainable Infrastructure
sources.verified_claim: London Plan Chapter 9 contains adopted policies on water infrastructure, flood risk and sustainable drainage, requiring development to address infrastructure and runoff issues; policy does not establish sample-parcel network headroom.

sources.title: London Sustainable Drainage Action Plan
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's SuDS Action Plan promotes new-development and retrofit drainage measures and notes growing population, land-use change and climate pressure on drains and sewers; regional action does not prove parcel capacity.

sources.title: 5. Creating a greener, healthier, and resilient city
sources.verified_claim: The July 2026 Draft London Plan includes draft policy GHR5 on flood risk and drainage among its greener, healthier and resilient-city policies; draft status is explicit and is not treated as adopted parcel policy.
